component.name: FrameXShot
component.summary: Fast, beautiful screenshot tool for Linux

description.p: FrameXShot is a fast, privacy-first screenshot tool for Linux. Capture a region, the full screen, a window or live OCR — then frame, annotate and polish the shot with backgrounds, effects and callouts before saving it to disk or copying it to the clipboard.
Everything runs locally: no cloud, no telemetry. Capture works on GNOME, KDE Plasma, COSMIC, wlroots compositors (Sway/Hyprland) and X11 desktops via automatic desktop-aware fallback chains.

Re-adds the StyleSelector to the Border section in the right sidebar. Eight frame styles are now available: Plain, Frosted (light frosted-glass like iOS sheets), Smoky (dark smoky-glass), Glow (warm orange edge glow), Raised (soft white photo mat), Carved (dark recessed frame), Outline (thin white trace), and Frame (bold picture frame). When a non-default style is selected, padding and opacity sliders appear to fine-tune the look. The chosen style, padding, and opacity persist via the top-of-sidebar "Set as Default" button. Existing capture chain (grim/slurp/hyprctl on Hyprland) and Linux install paths (Arch .pkg.tar.zst GPG-signed, .deb, .rpm, .flatpak, .dmg, .exe) are unchanged.

First proper release. Capture works end-to-end on CachyOS / Arch / Hyprland via system grim+slurp+hyprctl (no Flatpak sandbox, no portal). Native Arch .pkg.tar.zst is the recommended install path; .deb and .rpm available for Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora. AppImage was dropped because Tauri's bundled linuxdeploy ships binutils 2.35 which can't process CachyOS-era libraries with .relr.dyn relocations. The Flatpak still ships as a universal-fallback for non-Arch distros.
